frozen_flag_meaning: The manifest's frozen=true flag is the manifest-schema requirement that this selection is hash-pinned: every case file is bound to a SHA-256 of its raw working-tree bytes and the loader refuses the selection if any byte moves. It does NOT mean the benchmark is scientifically final, and it is not a qualification. The release status is release-candidate and the qualification status is UNQUALIFIED.
hash_basis: raw working-tree bytes, LF canonical checkout per docs/hash_basis_policy.md
preregistration_note: pilot-v7-rc4 is a release candidate and deliberately carries NO preregistration. Preregistration v3 remains bound to the frozen pilot-v6.1 benchmark and v1 to its own scope; both are unchanged and neither is extended to rc4. No preregistration v4 exists or is created by this phase.

supersedes.observation_note: pilot-v7-rc3 WAS observed by real models in the Phase-L-B QA-OFF requalification under the frozen protocol, and that evidence -- together with the Phase-N diagnosis of it -- is precisely what this redesign responds to. rc3 itself was not edited, its 102 classifications were not rescored, its HOLD was not retracted, and no rc4 task has been observed by any model.
supersedes.predecessor_evidence_protocol_note: Unlike Phase I, the Phase-L-B run executed the frozen 102-cell schedule exactly once under machine-enforced stop control, with no retry, replacement or resume, and terminated with the verdict the frozen rules produced. Its evidence is protocol-pristine; it is nevertheless NOT qualification evidence, because the verdict was HOLD.
supersedes.reason: Phase-O offline redesign of the pilot-v7-rc3 release candidate, built prospectively from the Phase-N forensic diagnosis of the Phase-L-B HOLD (docs/phaseN_phaseL_hold_forensic_diagnosis.md, verdict READY_FOR_RC4_OFFLINE_REDESIGN). Phase L-B executed all 102 formal cells of frozen rc3 exactly once and terminated SCHEDULE_COMPLETE_VERDICT_HOLD with nine invalidated cells; pilot-v7-rc3 remains UNQUALIFIED and every one of its classifications remains binding. Phase N attributed six of the nine invalidations to TOOL_SCHEMA_PRESENTATION_DEFECT -- the contract shown to the model advertised arguments as an unconstrained object while the sandbox enforced an undisclosed six-alias payload set, so a model could satisfy the advertised schema completely and still be refused -- and two more to HARNESS_FAILURE_ATTRIBUTION_DEFECT, in which an absorbing, order-independent row scalar masked a declared fault that had demonstrably fired with correct runtime provenance. Neither is a benchmark defect, and rc4 changes no task on their account. Twelve rc3 tasks are carried forward BYTE-IDENTICALLY, three carry a contract revision with unchanged bytes, and exactly two receive new IDs because their bytes change: BUD-014 -> BUD-017 and BUD-015 -> BUD-018, the only two tasks Phase N found to have failed benchmark reachability. PI-019 and BUD-016, whose zero exposure Phase N attributes to genuine model behaviour on reachable constructs, are deliberately NOT weakened. The instrument repairs live outside the benchmark: a truthful per-tool argument contract that the sandbox and the provider render from one table (iqa_soa.tools.argument_schema, tool-arguments-1), and ordered per-action failure telemetry (raw schema 5). No rc3, rc2, rc1 or pilot-v6.1 byte was edited, no Phase-L-B result was rescored, no seed was selected, and no model inference was performed. The frozen flag is the manifest-schema requirement that this selection is hash-pinned; it does NOT mean the benchmark is scientifically final. The release STATUS is release-candidate, the qualification status is UNQUALIFIED, and this release authorizes no execution.
